title: Social media publishing and listening
for: scheduling and publishing posts, post performance, mentions and listening on X, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky

manual.export: Export the post performance or analytics report as CSV from the scheduling tool or the network's own analytics (LinkedIn Page > Analytics > Export; X Analytics > Export data) and drop the file into the snapshots folder.

vendors.name: X (Twitter)
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__x`) until checked (the known writes are bookmarks and article publishing; posting via MCP is not confirmed)

The hosted server at https://api.x.com/mcp (announced June 2026) authenticates with the user's own X developer credentials; API tier limits apply to every call, and full-archive search needs a paid tier

The open-source xdevplatform/xmcp server runs locally with X_BEARER_TOKEN, X_OAUTH_CONSUMER_KEY and X_OAUTH_CONSUMER_SECRET but is not published as a versioned package, so no stdio entry; clone it if the hosted endpoint does not fit
The hosted URL comes from the X developer community announcement, not the API reference; confirm before wiring

auth.where: browser grant with an X Developer Platform app

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the app bearer token (developer.x.com > Keys and tokens) reads api.x.com/2/users/{id}/tweets with public_metrics for a scheduled performance snapshot

vendors.name: Buffer
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__buffer`) until checked
Buffer parks MCP-created posts as drafts or scheduled items ("you're the last step"), which fits the humans-decide rule; still, scheduling is a publish action
The vendor page confirms the server and OAuth or personal API key auth but does not print the endpoint URL; no .mcp.json entry until a person reads it from the Buffer settings page
Eleven channels including LinkedIn, X, Threads and Bluesky; every plan including Free; not in the Claude connectors directory

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the personal access token (Buffer > Settings > API) reads the GraphQL API for a scheduled post-performance snapshot

vendors.name: Hootsuite
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole servers (`mcp__hootsuite-publish`, `mcp__hootsuite-inbox`) until checked
Three servers: perch (publishing), nest (inbox), lumen (listening); wire only the ones a workflow needs, listening is read-only
Publishing through perch is a user-visible action; humans decide
Not in the Claude connectors directory

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; an OAuth token from a Hootsuite developer app reads platform.hootsuite.com/v1/messages for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Sprout Social
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__sproutsocial`) until checked (publishing over MCP is reported but not confirmed)
The endpoint comes from a secondary listing; Sprout's own page was not found, confirm before wiring

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; an API token (Settings > API) reads api.sproutsocial.com/v1/{customer_id}/analytics/posts for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Typefully
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__typefully`) until checked
Creating a draft is the safe write; scheduling publishes at the set time, so keep scheduling behind human approval

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the API key (Settings > Integrations) reads api.typefully.com/v1/drafts/recently-published for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Taplio
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__taplio`) until checked (publishing to LinkedIn is among the writes)
The endpoint comes from a secondary listing and the exact path was not confirmed; confirm before wiring

vendors.name: LinkedIn (organic pages and profiles)
caveats: No official LinkedIn MCP server; post and read pages through Buffer, Hootsuite, Typefully or Taplio above, or export Page analytics by hand
Community LinkedIn servers use unofficial APIs or browser automation and breach LinkedIn's terms; do not wire them
Public profile and company research goes through the Apify actors already wired (researcher skill), which is the scraping-search bridge

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; a Community Management API token (app with the Community Management product, partner approval) reads api.linkedin.com/rest/organizationalEntityShareStatistics for a scheduled page-performance snapshot

vendors.name: Ayrshare
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server until checked

The public server at https://www.ayrshare.com/docs/mcp is a read-only documentation search; the separate Action MCP that posts to 14+ networks with an API key is mentioned in the docs but its URL was not on the page read, so no .mcp.json entry
Posting through the Action server is a user-visible action; humans decide

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the API key (Ayrshare dashboard > API Key) reads app.ayrshare.com/api/analytics/post for a scheduled snapshot
